chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the benevolence of the man to his brother is that he accepts his gift, and that he should gift to him with what is with him, and he should not burden anything for him.'
And Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not like the ones who burden others.'

key_terms.الْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ: Those who burden others / those who are overly formal
key_terms.تُحْفَة: Gift, present, or token of affection
key_terms.يَتَكَلَّفَ: To burden / to impose difficulty / to be overly formal
key_terms.يُتْحِفَهُ: He gifts him / He gives a gift

ai.seo_question: What are the key etiquettes of giving and receiving gifts in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the spiritual etiquette of *takrimah* (honor) within the Shia concept of brotherhood, emphasizing that genuine respect is shown through gracious acceptance of gifts and reciprocal generosity without imposing undue burden or excessive formality. The Prophet’s declaration that he dislikes 'mutakallifin' (those who are overly formal or pretentious) underscores the Shia value of natural, sincere social bonds over rigid ceremonialism, reflecting the practical application of humility in communal life.
